gloss: the above; the aforementioned; what is written above (or to the right)

definitions.gloss: the above; the aforementioned; what is written above (or to the right)
definitions.explanation: A formal reference to content written above or previously in a document, originating from vertical right-to-left writing where earlier content appears to the right.

examples.japanese: {右記|うき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{通|とお}り→通り：01475_toori⟧⟦{申請|しんせい}します→申請する：25228_shinseisuru⟧。
{右記|うき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{内容|ないよう}→内容：01482_naiyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ご{確認|かくにん}→ご確認：23544_gokakunin⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
{右記|うき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{条件|じょうけん}→条件：03285_jouken⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{同意|どうい}する→同意する：06056_douisuru⟧⟦{場合|ばあい}→場合：01704_baai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{署名|しょめい}して→署名する：22432_shomeisuru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: If you agree to the conditions stated above, please sign.

notes:
{右|う} (right) + {記|き} (written). In traditional Japanese vertical writing, text flows from right to left, so earlier content is to the right. {右記|うき} therefore means "what was written previously" or "the above."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {右記|うき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{通|とお}り→通り：01475_toori⟧: as stated above
- {右記|うき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{住所|じゅうしょ}→住所：01430_juusho⟧: the address listed above
- {右記|うき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{条件|じょうけん}→条件：03285_jouken⟧: the conditions stated above
- {右記|うき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧とおり⟦{相違|そうい}→相違：04043_soui⟧⟦ありません→ある：00006_aru⟧: the above is correct without error

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{上記|じょうき}→上記：11375_jouki⟧: the above — used in horizontal writing (modern standard); functionally equivalent
- ⟦{下記|かき}→下記：11376_kaki⟧: the following, what is written below — the opposite, referring to content that comes after
- ⟦{左記|さき}→左記：17256_saki⟧: what follows (in vertical writing) — the counterpart to {右記|うき} in vertical text
- ⟦{前記|ぜんき}→前記：22210_zenki⟧: the aforementioned — refers to content mentioned previously

USAGE:
{右記|うき} is used primarily in formal documents, legal papers, and official forms that use vertical writing. In modern horizontal writing, ⟦{上記|じょうき}→上記：11375_jouki⟧ is more common. Both are formal register.
